agree.reason: The office log and the neighbouring district's results will persuade a sympathetic parent, but a board member who resists still has no real answer on athletics, and the early-drop-off fix has no cost attached.

honest.reason: It rightly avoids promising a graduation gain, but it adds facts the brief doesn't have: teens need 8–10 hours, they can't fall asleep before 11 p.m., they wake around 6, other districts faced the same scheduling problems, and the ice packs and crackers.

works_the_facts.reason: It derives 72 percent, one in six not graduating on time, $1,000 per school day and 'more than the next two combined', but it leaves the one-point attendance gain unconverted and doesn't state the first-period load as more than double the average of the next two periods.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is shown fairly through the visit log and survey, and the neighbouring district is used as the before-and-after case, but staying at 7:25 is never stated as an ongoing cost the way the bus money is.

qualification.reason: The pledge to track attendance, tardies and graduation has no target number, no reporting date and no consequence if the results don't come.

objections.reason: Cost and drop-off get concrete responses, but athletics is passed to 'ask our neighbors', which leaves the athletic director's after-dark and missed-class concerns largely unmet.

fit.reason: It is a proper op-ed with a headline and byline, comes in under 650 words, and is timed to the April 14 vote; it does soften the requested graduation claim, which is justified, and its placeholders still need filling.
